info.title: pannelAI API
info.summary: Management and data-plane API for the pannelAI gateway.
info.description: OpenAPI 3.1 contract for app-serv. Management routes use the pannel_session cookie. Data-plane routes use a gateway key when settings.security.require_api_key is enabled. Error envelopes are defined by the ManagementError and DataPlaneError schemas.

gatewayKey.description: Gateway key created through the management API.

ChatRequestMessage.description: One request turn. content may be omitted only for an assistant turn that carries tool_calls.

source.description: Where the list came from, "upstream" or "registry".

warning.description: Why the list is not from the upstream, when it is not.

QuotaWindowList.description: Paged over provider groups (docs/PORT/006-PORT-QUOTA-PAGING.md D1); per_page counts provider groups on this route, and one page carries every window of the page's groups.

QuotaEndpointDetail.description: The stored cap (null when none is set) plus every window for one endpoint.

UsageLiveActive.description: One request the gateway is routing right now.

UsageLiveFrame.description:
One `data:` payload of the live Usage stream. Full state rather than a delta, so a client that
missed a frame recovers on the next one. Both lists are always arrays, never null: an empty
in-flight set is a fact and `null` would be a second spelling of it.

active.description: The in-flight set, oldest first, so the longest-running request is the first row.

recent.description: The requests that just finished, newest first, bounded by the gateway.

error_provider.description: The provider the gateway last reported an error for, or an empty string.

fallback_strategy.description: The credential rotation default for every provider (SPEC-API-001 7.5).

provider_strategies.description: Per-provider overrides, keyed by provider id. Sent whole; an absent entry inherits the global default.

ProviderStrategyPatch.description: One provider's override. An entry must set at least one field; deleting the entry is how a provider returns to the global default.

provider_proxies.description: Per-provider proxy bindings, keyed by provider id. Sent whole; an absent entry inherits the global setting, `__none__` dials direct, and any other pool_id names a stored proxy row to try first.

ProviderProxyPatch.description: One provider's proxy binding. An entry must set at least one field; deleting the entry is how a provider returns to the global setting.

ProviderStatusSummary.description: Endpoint counts per state for one provider.

latency_ms.description: Sum of every matched request's own duration in milliseconds, so it grows with the request count. latency_p50_ms and latency_p95_ms carry the per-request picture.

latency_p50_ms.description: Median latency over the matched requests, in milliseconds.

latency_p95_ms.description: 95th percentile latency over the matched requests, in milliseconds.

latency_ms.description: This request's own duration in milliseconds. Unlike UsageTotals.latency_ms, which sums a window, this field measures one call.

fallback_strategy.description: The effective global default, never an empty string.

provider_strategies.description: The stored overrides, rendered as {} rather than null when there are none.

ProviderStrategyResponse.description: One provider's stored override. An absent field inherits the global default, so the panel renders what is stored rather than a filled-in copy.

provider_proxies.description: The stored bindings, rendered as {} rather than null when there are none.

ProviderProxyResponse.description: One provider's stored binding. An absent field inherits the global setting, so the panel renders what is stored rather than a filled-in copy.

get.summary: Live stream of what the gateway is routing now
get.description:
Server-sent events. Each frame is full state for the three facts a period window cannot carry:
the requests in flight now, the requests that just finished, and the provider the gateway last
reported an error for. A frame is sent when that state changes, and an idle connection receives
an SSE comment (`: ping`) rather than a frame, so a client counting frames is never told a change
happened. The status line and the SSE headers are committed with the first frame, so a failure
before it is an ordinary HTTP error in the management envelope.

200.description: An SSE stream of live frames.
